headline: Teele Square fire displaces 43 Somerville residents and closes six businesses
dek: A five-alarm blaze damaged 32 homes and a row of ground-floor businesses Wednesday; the city and Somerville Homeless Coalition have opened an emergency fund as the cause remains under investigation.
body: Somerville officials and the Somerville Homeless Coalition have activated an emergency fund for 43 residents displaced by a five-alarm fire that damaged a Teele Square building Wednesday. The City of Somerville said Thursday that the blaze affected 32 homes at 1137-1147 Broadway, and that every resident escaped safely. City staff and the American Red Cross were helping residents find temporary accommodations and meet immediate needs.

The fire began around 4:50 p.m. September 30 and continued for more than three hours, according to the Cambridge-Somerville Independent (https://csindie.com/more-than-40-people-are-displaced-after-teele-square-fire-chief-says/). The three-story brick building, also described in reports as 1135 Broadway, suffered heavy fire, smoke and water damage on its third floor and roof. The lower floors sustained extensive water damage, leaving all 32 units uninhabitable while the building is assessed and secured.

The damage also shut down the building’s ground-floor retail space. The Independent identified the affected businesses as Blue Moon smoke shop, Teele Square Coin Laundry, the Happy Crab and Masala restaurants, and Al-Aswad Dental; it reported that a liquor store at the far end of the building remained open. CBS Boston (https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/somerville-teele-square-building-fire/) described six businesses as destroyed and reported that the building was a total loss. The differing descriptions reflect that the damage assessment was still developing, but both accounts point to a major interruption for a commercial corner that serves nearby residents.

The response was unusually close to home for Somerville firefighters. The city’s Teele Square station is across the street, and Chief Charles Breen told CBS Boston that firefighters returning from another call saw smoke and heard the building’s alarm. Crews from neighboring departments were called in for mutual aid. The Independent reported that five aerial ladders were used to open the roof and ventilate the structure, with assistance from departments in Cambridge, Arlington, Boston, Brookline, Belmont, Chelsea, Everett, Malden, Medford, Revere and Watertown.

Several firefighters suffered minor injuries, according to the Independent, and two cats were found and removed safely. No residents were reported killed. The cause had not been determined as of Thursday, and Breen said the fire remained under investigation. That leaves questions about how the blaze spread through the roof and whether any code, electrical or other building-system issues contributed unanswered for now.

The immediate problem for residents is not only finding a place to stay but replacing household necessities while a building with 32 homes remains closed. Somerville’s Emergency Displacement Fund provides direct financial assistance to residents displaced by fires and other emergencies. The city said Thursday that it is seeking financial donations through the Somerville Homeless Coalition fund, rather than donated goods, while city workers and the Red Cross coordinate assistance.

The fire also adds a second recovery story to a block that has carried the effects of an earlier blaze for years. The Independent reported that a vacant lot known locally as “The Pit,” across from the damaged building, has remained empty since a 2011 fire. A hotel proposal for that site was before the city’s Zoning Board of Appeals on the same day as Wednesday’s fire, according to the paper. That overlap does not establish a connection between the projects or the fires, but it underscores how a single emergency can affect a neighborhood already waiting on redevelopment.

Somerville Mayor Jake Wilson told CBS Boston that the city wants to work with property owners, tenants and business owners on a faster recovery. No reconstruction schedule or final damage estimate had been announced by Thursday. For now, the confirmed next steps are temporary housing and emergency aid for displaced residents, continued fire investigation, and a broader assessment of which businesses and homes can be repaired or must be rebuilt.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Teele Square fire displaces 43 Somerville residents
seoDescription: A five-alarm Teele Square fire damaged 32 Somerville homes and closed six businesses; the city opened emergency aid as the cause remains under investigation.
